result.summary: The street environment features wide sidewalks and commercial land use but lacks essential pedestrian crossing infrastructure. No marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or traffic calming measures are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross a wide roadway with faded lane markings and potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks despite the presence of commercial storefronts on both sides of the street, creating an unpredictable environment for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire roadway width in the foreground and mid-ground.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The roadway is wide with multiple lanes including parking/turn lanes, increasing the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic while crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: The full width of the asphalt roadway.

hazards.name: Faded lane markings
hazards.description: The center line and other pavement markings are significantly faded, which can lead to driver confusion and lane drift.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians by moving them past parked cars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure, such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps, at an urban intersection. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the roadway and walkway surfaces show signs of wear and debris, and parked vehicles may obstruct sightlines for those attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the roadway without any designated markings or priority, increasing the risk of conflict with vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line can block the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right and left curbs near the intersection

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven road and sidewalk surfaces can create tripping hazards or cause pedestrians to deviate from their path.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the roadway and right-side sidewalk

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to ensure accessibility for all users.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image depicts a mixed-use urban intersection with sidewalks but a total absence of pedestrian crossing infrastructure. Pedestrians must cross an unmarked, multi-lane roadway without the protection of crosswalks, signals, or traffic control devices.
